comments.body:
## The evidence set this ticket was waiting for now EXISTS — and it changes the question

The plan reads "accumulate a representative set of real advisory review outcomes over time",
which scans as blocked on the passage of time. It is not. Measured from the ticket store
2026-08-05, across all 3,299 ticket dirs.

## Sampling window and method (AC1)

Two distinct numbers; conflating them is the easy mistake:

- **51 review-result events MENTION `project.review-phase-boundaries`** — reviews where the
  criterion was in scope, carried in the registry/checklist.
- **6 contain an actual FINDING citing it**, across 6 distinct tickets.

Fire rate ~12% of in-scope reviews.

## Impact distribution — the decisive number

    impact 0.0  ->  4 findings
    impact 0.4  ->  1 finding
    impact 0.5  ->  1 finding
    -----------------------------------
    max observed 0.5   |   blocking threshold 0.90

**No finding has ever come within 0.4 of the threshold.** That reframes this ticket's question.
Flipping `blocking_enabled` at 0.90 would change NOTHING — no historical finding would have
blocked. The real question is whether 0.90 is the right threshold given an observed impact
ceiling of 0.5.

## Finding quality — no obvious false positive in the sample

Specific and substantively correct. Verbatim:

- 1eee: "The new ac-satisfiability rubric — explicitly applied by the Pass-1 finder — instructs
  it to assign severity (MAJOR/MINOR), which is the deterministic outcome work owned by Pass-3."
- 7cf9: "Changed G7 rubric directs the discovery-phase reviewer to make a dedup/drop decision ...
  which is deterministic-decision (Pass-3) work."
- 8cea: "The new no-file-impact Pass-1 criterion rubric directs the evaluator to decide the
  review outcome (Return PASS), which is Pass-3 deterministic-decision work."

Each names a concrete rubric and the boundary it crosses. The criterion is doing its job.

## Options (AC2)

The criterion is USEFUL but consistently SUB-THRESHOLD:

1. **Keep advisory, keep the threshold.** Findings are real but low-impact by their own scoring.
   Honest, costs nothing, changes nothing.
2. **Keep advisory, LOWER the threshold** so 0.4-0.5 findings surface more prominently without
   blocking. Fixes the mismatch between observed impact and configured threshold, no author
   friction.
3. **Promote to blocking AND lower to ~0.4.** Only this blocks anything. Volume is low (6 over
   the window) so author impact would be small — but it makes a phase-boundary violation a hard
   stop on six data points, none rated above 0.5 by its own scorer.

## Caveats — do not over-read this

- 6 findings is a small sample. One high-impact miss would change the picture.
- I judged the findings "appear correct" by READING them. That is not the same as confirming with
  each author that the finding was actionable, which is what AC2's "false positives" and "author
  impact" actually ask for.
- Impact scores are self-reported by the reviewer that produced them, so "max 0.5" is the
  criterion's own view of its severity, not an independent judgement.

AC3 (any routing change lands through an independently reviewed ticket and Gerrit change) is
unaffected and still applies to whichever option is chosen.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

`project.review-phase-boundaries` runs advisory. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json:82-87` holds
`"default_posture": "advisory"`, `"block_threshold": 0.9`, `"blocking_enabled": false`.

The sampling already recorded on this ticket (2026-08-05) covered 51 in-scope reviews and found 6
findings with a maximum author impact of **0.5**, against a 0.90 block threshold. That measurement
settles one thing decisively: **flipping `blocking_enabled` at the current 0.90 threshold would
change nothing** — no observed finding has ever come within 0.4 of the line. So "enable blocking"
and "keep advisory" are not the real choice; the real choice is what threshold, if any, makes this
criterion load-bearing without punishing authors.

**Operator direction (2026-08-09):** do not pick a posture from the current sample. First assess the
HISTORICAL IMPACT of lowering the threshold — i.e. counter-factually replay what would have been
blocked at candidate thresholds — and choose from that evidence.

A caveat carried forward from the existing sampling comment, which the analysis must resolve rather
than inherit: the 6 findings were never confirmed against false positives. A threshold chosen from
a finding set that includes false positives would block authors on reviewer noise.

Related and directly instructive: ticket `f391`'s analysis of the `undecomposed` axis showed that
this codebase's persisted `*-REVIEW_RESULT.json` sidecar stream under `.tickets-tracker/` supports
exactly this kind of counter-factual replay at **zero LLM cost**, and that an impact floor applied
without regard to grade silently makes a low-graded finding block like a high-graded one. Use the
same replay instrument here, and check for the same failure mode.

## Plan

Replay the persisted review corpus and, for each candidate `block_threshold`, compute what WOULD
have blocked: how many changes, on which tickets, and with what author-visible impact scores. Then
audit the findings that a candidate threshold would newly make blocking — every one of them — for
false positives, since those are precisely the cases that would have stopped an author.

Report the trade-off curve rather than a single number, then record a posture decision (threshold
value and `blocking_enabled`) justified by that curve.

Do NOT change `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` in this ticket. Landing a routing/posture change is a
separate reviewable change, and coupling the analysis to the config edit would make the evidence
hard to review on its own merits.

## Testing

This is an analysis ticket: its deliverable is a recorded readout, not code. Verification is that
the numbers are reproducible — state the corpus location, the replay method, and the exact
denominator, so a second reader can re-derive the curve. Never estimate a rate whose denominator is
not reachable from the checkout; say so instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The counter-factual replay is recorded: for each candidate `block_threshold`, the number of
      reviews and distinct tickets that would have been blocked, with the corpus size and the exact
      denominator stated.
- [ ] Every finding that a candidate threshold would newly make BLOCKING is audited for false
      positives, and the false-positive rate among them is reported.
- [ ] The readout states whether impact is applied grade-independently for this criterion (the
      failure mode `f391` found on the `undecomposed` axis), since a grade-independent floor would
      make any threshold choice misleading.
- [ ] A posture decision is recorded — threshold value and whether `blocking_enabled` flips —
      justified by the curve and the false-positive audit, not by the 51-review sample alone.
- [ ] The readout has a Limits section separating verified observations from what the reachable
      corpus could not answer.
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` is UNCHANGED by this ticket; any posture change is filed as a
      separate follow-up ticket linked `discovered_from`.
